problem:
Problem description
- There is a single-period staffing allocation problem with two indexed sets: branches $$\mathcal R$$ and specialties $$\mathcal S$$. Applicant groups are indexed by $$\mathcal T$$.
- Each branch-specialty pair has a required demand represented by the parameter $$d_{r,s}$$ for every $$r \in \mathcal R$$ and $$s \in \mathcal S$$.
- Each applicant type has an available headcount represented by the parameter $$n_t$$ for every $$t \in \mathcal T$$.
- Each applicant type $$t$$ can only be assigned to a subset of specialties, denoted by $$\mathcal S_t^{\mathrm{cap}} \subseteq \mathcal S$$.
- Each applicant type $$t$$ has one preferred specialty, denoted by $$s_t^{\mathrm{pref}} \in \mathcal S$$, and one preferred branch, denoted by $$r_t^{\mathrm{pref}} \in \mathcal R$$.
- The planning priorities are lexicographic and ordered as $$p_1 \succ p_2 \succ p_3$$.
- Priority $$p_1$$ means that staffing demand for all branch-specialty requirements should be satisfied as fully as possible.
- Priority $$p_2$$ means that as many recruited people as possible should be placed in their preferred specialty, up to the target count $$Q_2$$.
- Priority $$p_3$$ means that as many recruited people as possible should be placed in their preferred branch, up to the target count $$Q_3$$.
- The planning goal is to find an assignment that respects applicant availability and capability limits while optimizing the priorities in order.
- Assignments that violate an applicant type’s allowed specialties are not permitted.
- No applicant type may be used beyond its available number $$n_t$$.
- Demand shortfalls, specialty-preference shortfalls, and branch-preference shortfalls are tracked as deviation quantities for the goal-planning hierarchy.
- A solution is represented by:
  - $$x_{t,r,s}$$: the number of applicants of type $$t$$ assigned to branch $$r$$ in specialty $$s$$.
  - $$u_{r,s}$$: the unmet demand remaining for branch $$r$$ and specialty $$s$$.
  - $$v_2$$: the shortfall from the preferred-specialty target $$Q_2$$.
  - $$v_3$$: the shortfall from the preferred-branch target $$Q_3$$.
  - Optional reporting quantities may include the number of assigned applicants who satisfy $$p_2$$ and the number who satisfy $$p_3$$.

Input Format
{
  "branches": "$$\\mathcal R$$, the set of branch locations",
  "specialties": "$$\\mathcal S$$, the set of professional specialties",
  "applicant_types": "$$\\mathcal T$$, the set of applicant categories",
  "demand": "matrix $$d_{r,s}$$ with shape $$R \\times S$$, where $$d_{r,s}$$ is the required headcount of specialty $$s$$ at branch $$r$$",
  "available_supply": "vector $$n_t$$ with shape $$T$$, where $$n_t$$ is the number of applicants of type $$t$$",
  "feasible_specialties": "list $$\\mathcal S_t^{\\mathrm{cap}}$$ for each $$t \\in \\mathcal T$$, giving the specialties that type $$t$$ can handle",
  "preferred_specialty": "vector $$s_t^{\\mathrm{pref}}$$ with shape $$T$$, where $$s_t^{\\mathrm{pref}}$$ is the preferred specialty of type $$t$$",
  "preferred_branch": "vector $$r_t^{\\mathrm{pref}}$$ with shape $$T$$, where $$r_t^{\\mathrm{pref}}$$ is the preferred branch of type $$t$$",
  "priority_levels": ["$$p_1$$", "$$p_2$$", "$$p_3$$"],
  "priority_targets": {
    "preferred_specialty_target": "$$Q_2$$, the target number of recruits whose assigned specialty matches their preference",
    "preferred_branch_target": "$$Q_3$$, the target number of recruits whose assigned branch matches their preference"
  }
}

Output Format
{
  "assignment": "tensor $$x_{t,r,s}$$ with shape $$T \\times R \\times S$$, giving the number of applicants of type $$t$$ assigned to branch $$r$$ and specialty $$s$$",
  "unmet_demand": "matrix $$u_{r,s}$$ with shape $$R \\times S$$, giving the remaining unmet demand after assignment",
  "priority_shortfall": {
    "p_1": "overall demand shortfall summary for priority $$p_1$$",
    "p_2": "shortfall $$v_2$$ from the preferred-specialty target $$Q_2$$",
    "p_3": "shortfall $$v_3$$ from the preferred-branch target $$Q_3$$"
  },
  "priority_attainment_report": {
    "preferred_specialty_matches": "count of assigned applicants whose specialty matches $$s_t^{\\mathrm{pref}}$$",
    "preferred_branch_matches": "count of assigned applicants whose branch matches $$r_t^{\\mathrm{pref}}$$"
  }
}

Example(s)

Input 1
{
  "branches": ["Donghai City", "Nanjiang City"],
  "specialties": [$$1$$, $$2$$, $$3$$],
  "applicant_types": [$$1$$, $$2$$, $$3$$, $$4$$, $$5$$, $$6$$],
  "demand": {
    "Donghai City": {
      $$1$$: $$1000$$,
      $$2$$: $$2000$$,
      $$3$$: $$1500$$
    },
    "Nanjiang City": {
      $$1$$: $$2000$$,
      $$2$$: $$1000$$,
      $$3$$: $$1000$$
    }
  },
  "available_supply": {
    $$1$$: $$1500$$,
    $$2$$: $$1500$$,
    $$3$$: $$1500$$,
    $$4$$: $$1500$$,
    $$5$$: $$1500$$,
    $$6$$: $$1500$$
  },
  "feasible_specialties": {
    $$1$$: [$$1$$, $$2$$],
    $$2$$: [$$2$$, $$3$$],
    $$3$$: [$$1$$, $$3$$],
    $$4$$: [$$1$$, $$3$$],
    $$5$$: [$$2$$, $$3$$],
    $$6$$: [$$3$$]
  },
  "preferred_specialty": {
    $$1$$: $$1$$,
    $$2$$: $$2$$,
    $$3$$: $$1$$,
    $$4$$: $$3$$,
    $$5$$: $$3$$,
    $$6$$: $$3$$
  },
  "preferred_branch": {
    $$1$$: "Donghai City",
    $$2$$: "Donghai City",
    $$3$$: "Nanjiang City",
    $$4$$: "Nanjiang City",
    $$5$$: "Donghai City",
    $$6$$: "Nanjiang City"
  },
  "priority_targets": {
    "preferred_specialty_target": $$8000$$,
    "preferred_branch_target": $$8000$$
  }
}

parameters.name: demand
parameters.description: Required demand for each branch-specialty pair

parameters.name: available_supply
parameters.description: Available headcount for each applicant type

parameters.name: feasible_specialties
parameters.description: Feasible specialty subset for each applicant type

parameters.name: preferred_specialty
parameters.description: Preferred specialty for each applicant type

parameters.name: preferred_branch
parameters.description: Preferred branch for each applicant type

parameters.name: preferred_specialty_target
parameters.description: Target number of applicants placed in their preferred specialty

parameters.name: preferred_branch_target
parameters.description: Target number of applicants placed in their preferred branch

variables.name: assignment
variables.description: Number of applicants of type t assigned to branch r in specialty s

variables.name: unmet_demand
variables.description: Unmet demand for each branch-specialty pair

constraints.name: assignment_type_capacity
constraints.description: Assignments are only permitted to specialties allowed for each applicant type.

constraints.name: assignment_supply_limit
constraints.description: The total number of applicants assigned for each type cannot exceed its available supply.

constraints.name: nonnegative_unmet_demand
constraints.description: Unmet demand values must be nonnegative.

constraints.name: nonnegative_preference_shortfalls
constraints.description: Preference shortfall variables must be nonnegative.

constraints.name: demand_shortfall_tracking
constraints.description: Each branch-specialty demand is matched by assigned applicants plus unmet demand, with no overstaffing.

constraints.name: lexicographic_priority_order
constraints.description: Objectives are optimized in the order demand satisfaction, preferred specialty attainment, then preferred branch attainment.

constraints.name: preferred_specialty_shortfall_definition
constraints.description: The shortfall from the preferred-specialty target equals target minus the number of assigned applicants placed in their preferred specialty.

constraints.name: preferred_branch_shortfall_definition
constraints.description: The shortfall from the preferred-branch target equals target minus the number of assigned applicants placed in their preferred branch.

constraints.name: nonnegative_integer_assignment_domain
constraints.description: Assignment variables must be nonnegative integers.

objectives.name: lexicographic_demand_and_preference_satisfaction
objectives.description: Lexicographically prioritize satisfying staffing demand as fully as possible, then maximize placement in preferred specialties up to the target, then maximize placement in preferred branches up to the target.

final_objective.description: Use preemption optimization to prioritize minimizing total unmet staffing demand first, then minimizing preferred-specialty shortfall, and finally minimizing preferred-branch shortfall, reflecting lexicographic priorities p_1 \succ p_2 \succ p_3.
